issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# PoemWorld: a three-role world that writes a short poem

Make a new domain for HuTian: PoemWorld, the smallest world that is still a whole world. From a request it writes a short poem, and the system releases the poem once it is approved.

What to make:

- A domain package `poemworld` (command `poemworld`, world id prefix `pw`) beside the seven domains under `src/`, added the way `DEV.md` says a domain is added: its definition through the `hutian.definitions` entry point, its organization graph in `assets/` in Chinese and English, its system and worker images, and its place in `install.sh`, the CI workflows and the per-domain checks.
- Three roles, one of each category a definition needs: `poet` makes the poem (`poem.md`) from the world's input; `editor` assesses it against the input, asks the poet for changes when it falls short, and approves each version; `reader` uses it: it reads each version the world publishes and says how the poem reads, which the poet and the editor watch. One edge, poet and editor. The release is the poem the editor approved last.
- Keep it small: the roles, their contracts and the release gate make it a world, not features.

Where it goes: one pull request to the private repository `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base branch `dev`, which holds HuTian's code. Merging it is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: on `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted in a new directory, build its images there from that version (older images on the machine are not that version), run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh PoemWorld world with the input "Write a four-line poem about the first snow." to its release. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token that trial-machine's commands get as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2` (give their provider `auth` `claude-oauth` and `credential_env` `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2`), with at most 16 executions and 2000 model seconds: a simple task, a cheap worker and a small budget are enough to show the world works. The pull request says what was made and how the trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, and the poem.

comments.body:
Acceptance and release-gate criteria for PoemWorld:

1. I compare the exact builder PR head against the World objective and architect Brief. The delivery must contain the poemworld package beside the existing domains, the poemworld command and pw id prefix, hutian.definitions registration, Chinese and English organization assets, system and worker images, and install.sh/CI/per-domain-check integration. The graph must define exactly poet, editor, and reader in the required categories, with only the poet-editor edge. Poet writes poem.md from input; editor assesses against input, requests changes when needed, and approves each version; reader reads published versions and reports feedback watched by poet/editor. Reader feedback is not an additional release gate.

2. Before approving a PR into release, I require a merge-clean head, passing repository regression checks, and evidence that installation succeeds and the kernel reads the definition. The version is worth trial only when editor approval is represented as the release gate in the definition/contracts and the delivery has no missing owned path.

3. For final acceptance, the exact head must also have an operator trial of that version: a fresh trial-machine install directory; images built from that checkout/version rather than cached older images; regression checks run where Docker is available; Claude Code worker configuration claude-sonnet-5-5 at low effort with auth claude-oauth and credential_env CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2; no more than 16 executions and 2000 model seconds; and a fresh pw world using the exact first-snow prompt. The operator record must name the trial world id, installed version/world-result release, release event, and released poem, which must be four lines about first snow. It must include the current trial logs/records and diagnosis of every problem by layer (world, position, domain implementation, kernel, or worker), with non-worker findings handed to their owner and worker-only findings captured as a draft objective. A diagnosis that still describes pre-trial state, or an unresolved world/position/domain/kernel problem, blocks final approval.

4. I inspect the records myself and approve only the exact PR commit tested. A push after approval requires review again. The final delivery must be present in the repository/PR that will be delivered to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian on dev; the maintainer retains the merge decision. Missing, skipped, or cached checks are not passes.
